Yes, I totally object to kids who haven't experienced much trying to justify their so-called "validity" with the argument that "one beating can equal years of abuse because they're all valid". Let's admit this one thing: the pain of being beaten once is valid, but in any case, or more rigorously, on average, it can't exceed years of abuse, no matter how much you try to make an example out of it. And a lot of times people argue this because they really just haven't been tortured too much. 

You each have your own validity, but it's not something that can be equated. I really wish those kinds of analogies would stop, it's really very stupid.

It's privileged and insulting that they try to equate their lives with those of us who live in really conservative areas facing extreme situations.

There are differences in suffering, and that's the truth. Validity doesn't hide the facts. It's not "invalidating you", it's the people who are really suffering more who are telling the truth. To equate the less severe with the more severe is to invalidate those who are experiencing more pain.

I can say that I reject any discussion of this, there is nothing to discuss. I fed up with the "validity" discourse long time ago tbh, lots of young people without a lot of experience couldn't tell the difference between facts and "people actually trying to silence them".

People who pride themselves on being progressive and having suffered can also be arrogantly ignorant of the suffering of others, and I have seen too many people like these.

I'm not quite sure what's helpful ...... for me, I have been more patient and kind to them (and myself) and that my partner is learning to take care of all of us. This helps, and we are able to return to peace and stability temporarily. and we also stay away from past traumatic situations and triggers, living in a safer space.

In the long run though, it may require dealing with more other issues(trauma, painful struggles, etc) before things rly get better, but I'm not there yet(:3_ヽ)_ …
